original_question: Let M = M(X, a)^Gamma with a a finite-dimensional associative algebra. Go beyond the classification of irreducible finite-dimensional M-modules and describe all indecomposable finite-dimensional modules, together with the block decomposition of the finite-dimensional module category.
target_in_paper: Section 4.2.3, "Indecomposable modules": in the general EMA subsection, after recalling the associative classification in Theorem 2.1, the paper asks for a description of all indecomposable finite-dimensional modules and the block decomposition of the finite-dimensional module category for M = M(X,a)^Γ. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the associative EMA setting M = M(X,a)^Γ, takes the classification of irreducible finite-dimensional modules as the starting point, and asks for exactly the two next problems named in the paper: classification of indecomposable finite-dimensional modules and block decomposition of the finite-dimensional module category. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s standing setup should be stated: k is algebraically closed; X = Spec A is an affine scheme over k; and Γ is a finite group acting on X (equivalently on A) and on a by algebra automorphisms. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))

Because Section 4.2.3 explicitly refers back to Theorem 2.1, a should be specified as a finite-dimensional unital associative k-algebra, not just an arbitrary associative algebra. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))

In §§1–2 the paper also assumes that |Γ| is not divisible by char(k); this is part of the ambient hypotheses for the associative EMA framework. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))

To make M fully explicit, one should say that M(X,a)^Γ is the algebra of Γ-equivariant regular maps X → a, equivalently the fixed-point subalgebra of a ⊗ A under the diagonal Γ-action. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))

The relevant category whose blocks are sought is the category of finite-dimensional M-modules over k; the paper does not broaden this question to infinite-dimensional modules in Section 4.2.3. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))

No extra hypotheses such as freeness of the Γ-action, semisimplicity of a, or Lie-specific assumptions belong in this associative open problem; those occur elsewhere in the survey. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field, let X = Spec A be an affine scheme over k, let a be a finite-dimensional unital associative k-algebra, and let Γ be a finite group acting on X and on a by algebra automorphisms, with |Γ| not divisible by char(k). Set M = M(X,a)^Γ, the associative equivariant map algebra of Γ-equivariant regular maps X → a. The irreducible finite-dimensional M-modules are already classified in Section 2. Can one classify all indecomposable finite-dimensional M-modules and determine the block decomposition of the category of finite-dimensional M-modules? ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))
justification: This is the closest paper-faithful sharpening of your draft because Section 4.2.3 states precisely this associative open problem and does not ask for anything broader. I kept the problem in the general associative EMA setting of Sections 1–2 and 4.2, rather than drifting into the more specialized Lie-theoretic questions of Section 4.3.1. I also made explicit the standing hypotheses and the meaning of M, since those are implicit in the paper’s formulation but needed for a stand-alone question. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))
